Financing equipment-dependent service SMEs: a systematic literature review

Abstract
This systematic literature review follows PRISMA 2020 and covers 64 studies published from 2000 to 2025.

1. Introduction
Paragraph 1 on SME financing describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on SME financing describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

2. Methods
We searched Scopus and Web of Science. Records identified: 1,212; after duplicates removed: 980; screened: 980; full texts assessed: 160; included: 64. Paragraph 1 on screening describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on screening describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

3. Results
Most included studies use survey data (n = 38). Survival is higher among studios still operating today. Paragraph 1 on synthesis describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

4. Discussion
Paragraph 1 on gaps describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on gaps describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

5. Conclusion
Evidence on financing is thin for service SMEs.
